title: autotrade — discovery on minute bars (scalping)
_why: Run once to create the first scalping rule, then let revise improve it nightly.
Minute bars, not daily: a rule measured on daily bars and traded on one-minute bars was
measured on a different thing. yfinance gives 7 days of 1m — around 2,700 bars per symbol,
enough trades for a win rate to mean something at this frequency.
Costs are on by default and they dominate here. A round trip pays commission both ways plus
0.18% transaction tax on the sell, so a scalping rule has to clear roughly 0.2% before it has
made anything. Most candidates will be refused for that, and that refusal is the point.
The confirmation symbols are held out of the selection entirely — a rule is chosen on the
first three and scored on the last two.

pipeline.instruction:
You are choosing where to search for a SCALPING rule on one-minute bars — a position held minutes, not days. Answer with a JSON object only, no prose.

Shape:
{"families":[...],"fast":[...],"slow":[...],"low":[...],"high":[...],"stopLossPct":[...],"takeProfitPct":[...],"holdout":0.3}

families is any of: ma-cross, ema-cross, rsi, bollinger, macd. Periods are counted in one-minute bars, so what would be 5 and 20 on daily bars is far too slow here — think in the range of a few minutes to an hour. Stops and targets must be small and real: a round trip costs about 0.2% in commission and tax, so a target under that cannot make money no matter how often it hits.

Read the history of refusals. A combination refused for too few trades will be refused again at the same parameters; faster periods trade more. Keep the space under about 150 combinations.

_note: Symbols are typed by hand for the MVP — no screening condition, so nothing has to be
created in HTS first. The intraday pipeline (pipeline.example.json) fetches one symbol's
minute bars, so keep its stk_cd and the trade's symbol the same until the loop can carry
mock, not real: the account decides, and a paper-stage rule cannot reach live money anyway.
